newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian government accused of protecting Rao.
newsitem.headline: Indian government accused of protecting Rao.

text.p: India's main opposition party accused the government on Tuesday of shielding former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in a criminal case to check a potential threat to the ruling coalition.
The Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) made the allegations after a government prosecutor investigating criminal conspiracy accusations aimed at Rao resigned from the case.

News agencies said Gopal Subramaniam, senior counsel for the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), quit the case on Monday after receiving government instructions to bow to an expected demand by Rao for bail in the $100,000 criminal cheating case.
The agencies quoted Subramaniam as saying he objected to "political pressure".
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority centre-left coalition depends on the support of Rao's Congress party to survive in parliament.
BJP spokesman Yashwant Sinha lauded Subramaniam's decision and accused the government of "blatant politicisation of the CBI for the sole purpose of shielding the former prime minister".
The BJP claimed Deve Gowda's government wanted to appease Congress in order to protect its hold on power.

The Communist Party of India, part of Deve Gowda's ruling coalition, condemned what it called the government's "interference in the functioning of the premier investigation agency of the country". The CBI is the federal police agency.

But Law Minister Ramakant Khalap said the government was entitled to take a stand in the case. "There was no reason to oppose the bail of Mr Rao if moved," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Khalap as saying.

Congress spokesman Vithal Gadgil said the government "was well within its rights" to instruct the CBI to acquiesce to Rao's expected bail application. "In hundreds of cases, the government gives such instructions," PTI quoted him as saying.
Rao and two others have been accused of trying to cheat an expatriate Indian businessman of $100,000 in 1983. Rao says he is innocent.
Rao had been scheduled to appear in court on Monday to face charges and possible arrest.

But the Supreme Court intervened, exempting the former prime minister from appearing in the local court until it rules on a police demand for a change in venue. The Supreme Court scheduled a hearing on the police request for next Monday.
Rao, who quit as Congress leader on September 21 after a judge upheld a summons to appear in court, had been expected to request bail if arrested at Monday's planned hearing.
Newspapers said Subramaniam, a private lawyer on the CBI's prosecution team, received a note from the CBI director early on Monday instructing him not to oppose any bid by Rao to win bail.
BJP officials said the government had told the CBI director to issue the instructions.

Subramaniam could not be reached for comment. A CBI spokesman had no information about the note. A government spokesman said the CBI was an independent agency and entitled to instruct its counsel whether or not to oppose a bail plea.
In a separate case, Rao won temporary respite when a Delhi court adjourned a hearing into forgery charges until Thursday.
Last week the CBI charged Rao and three others with attempting to tarnish the reputation of an opposition leader in 1989 through the use of forged documents.
